source_name: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 3 (Industrial Processes and Product Use)
read_from: Chapter 2 Tables 2.1, 2.4, 2.6 and Equations 2.4 and 2.8; Chapter 3 Tables 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9; Chapter 4 Tables 4.1, 4.2, 4.5, 4.10, 4.15, 4.20, 4.21, 4.24

carbonates.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of carbonate, at 100 percent calcination
carbonates.note: Use with the fraction actually calcined. A carbonate that leaves the kiln uncalcined has released nothing.

cement.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of clinker

clinker_emission_factor.note: 0.51 assumes clinker is 65 percent CaO, all of it from CaCO3, fully calcined. The 1.02 adds back the CO2 in cement kiln dust lost from the system; a plant that recycles all its dust uses 1.00.

cao_variants.note: Table text on page 2.12: for a clinker of known CaO content, before the kiln dust correction.

clinker_from_cement.note: Cement is not clinker. Where only cement tonnage is known, the clinker fraction of the product mix has to be applied, and imported clinker belongs to whoever made it.

lime.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of lime produced

default_mix.note: Equation 2.8: 85 percent high calcium at 0.75 plus 15 percent dolomitic at 0.77, where the split is not known.

glass.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of glass melted
glass.note: Cullet is recycled glass; it has already released its carbonate CO2, so the factor applies only to the virgin part of the batch.

tier1_default.note: 0.20 x (1 - 0.50). Use a measured cullet ratio where there is one.

ammonia.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of ammonia
ammonia.note: This is the CO2 from the fuel AND the feedstock together, which is how ammonia is reported. CO2 recovered for urea manufacture is subtracted, because it leaves as urea rather than to air.

average_natural_gas.note: European average over modern and older plants.

nitric_acid.unit: kg N2O per tonne of nitric acid, on 100 percent pure acid

nscr_all_processes.note: Non-selective catalytic reduction. The factor already counts the abatement; verify the unit is installed and ran all year.

adipic_acid.unit: kg N2O per tonne of adipic acid

destruction_factor.note: The share of the N2O an abatement technology destroys.

utilisation_factor.note: The share of the year the abatement system actually ran. Destruction times utilisation is what is abated; assuming 100 percent uptime understates the source.

calcium_carbide.note: Using the carbide - to make acetylene - releases its carbon too, and that is a separate line from making it.

titanium_dioxide.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of product

not_published.titanium_slag: IPCC publishes no default: only two plants make it and their data is confidential. A plant that makes it has to use its own reductant and carbothermal input.

iron_and_steel.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of the named product

direct_reduced_iron.note: Assumes natural gas, 12.5 GJ per tonne of DRI.

steel_basic_oxygen_furnace.note: Includes the blast furnace iron making.

steel_electric_arc_furnace.note: Steel from SCRAP. Not applicable to an EAF charged with pig iron - that iron's emissions belong to the blast furnace.

steel_open_hearth_furnace.note: Includes the blast furnace iron making.

steel_global_average.note: 65 percent BOF, 30 percent EAF, 5 percent OHF.

ferroalloys.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of product
ferroalloys.note: These factors assume fossil reductants. If any bio-carbon is used beyond woodchips in FeSi and Si-metal, they do not apply.

anode_co2.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of aluminium

pfc.note: Perfluorocarbons are made during an anode effect. CWPB is centre worked prebake, SWPB side worked prebake, VSS vertical stud Soderberg, HSS horizontal stud Soderberg.
pfc.caveat: The uncertainty on these runs from -99 to +380 percent for CWPB. They are for use only where no anode effect data exists; a smelter that records anode effect minutes should use the Tier 2 slope coefficients.

magnesium.unit: kg SF6 per tonne of magnesium cast
magnesium.note: The Tier 1 assumption is that all the SF6 bought is emitted. Where the foundry records its own consumption, that figure is better.

lead.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of lead
lead.default_note: 0.52 assumes 80 percent Imperial Smelting and 20 percent direct smelting. Use it only where the split is unknown.

zinc.unit: tonnes CO2 per tonne of zinc
zinc.default_note: 1.72 weights 60 percent Imperial Smelting and 40 percent Waelz kiln.

not_published.electro_thermic: IPCC records the electro-thermic factor as unknown.
